question:
Let $S$ be a subset of $\{1,2,3,...,50\}$ such that no pair of distinct elements in $S$ has a sum divisible by $7$. What is the maximum number of elements in $S$?
$\text{(A) } 6\quad \text{(B) } 7\quad \text{(C) } 14\quad \text{(D) } 22\quad \text{(E) } 23$
solution:
Group the numbers by their residues modulo 7. Since $50=7\cdot7+1$, residue 1 occurs 8 times and every other residue occurs 7 times.
The nonzero residues form three complementary pairs: $(1,6)$, $(2,5)$, and $(3,4)$. Taking a number from each side of any pair would give a sum divisible by 7, so these pairs contribute at most 8, 7, and 7 elements, respectively. At most one multiple of 7 is allowed, giving an upper bound of $8+7+7+1=23$.
This bound is attained by taking all numbers with residues 1, 2, or 3, together with 7: no two selected elements have residues summing to 0 modulo 7.
Final answer: 23
